content.value_statement: Teams need faster ways to understand competitor messaging across public ad libraries. This skill structures ad collection, theme analysis, and campaign insights for original marketing work.
actual_capabilities: Guides extraction of competitor ads from public ad libraries.
Organizes ad screenshots, copy, CTAs, formats, and themes.
Compares messaging patterns across one or more competitors.
Identifies common pain points, audiences, and value propositions.
Produces recommendations for original ad tests and positioning ideas.
limitations: Requires access to the relevant public ad libraries or exported ad data.
Cannot prove ad performance unless platforms expose reliable engagement data.
Does not guarantee compliance with each platform terms of service.
Insights should inspire original creative, not copied ads.

use_cases.title: Prepare Campaign Research
use_cases.description: Review competitor ads before planning a new campaign and summarize the strongest recurring messages.

use_cases.title: Map Market Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare several competitors to find positioning gaps, repeated promises, and audience segments.

use_cases.title: Build Creative Briefs
use_cases.description: Turn ad patterns into themes, creative references, and testable directions for new original ads.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Competitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner research for a single brand.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract current ads from [Competitor] in [Ad Library]. Summarize the main themes, CTAs, formats, and pain points.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review across a small competitive set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze ads from [Company A], [Company B], and [Company C]. Compare their messaging, audiences, and creative formats.

prompt_templates.title: Study a Specific Problem
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused analysis for one market pain point.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Competitor] ads that mention [Problem]. Identify the claims, proof points, objections, and creative angles used.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Campaign Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the collected ads for [Market]. Create a campaign brief with messaging gaps, test hypotheses, and original ad concepts.

output_examples.input: Analyze active Facebook ads from a project management competitor.
output: Summary of active themes such as collaboration, planning, and reporting.
CTA and format breakdown for static, video, and carousel ads.
Recommendations for original tests that address uncovered positioning gaps.

output_examples.input: Compare LinkedIn ads from three B2B software companies.
output: Competitor comparison by audience, pain point, and proof point.
Shared messaging patterns and areas where each brand differs.
Suggested creative brief directions for a differentiated campaign.

output_examples.input: Review competitor ads about onboarding and activation.
output: Pain point map showing friction, time to value, and team adoption themes.
Copy patterns that emphasize outcomes instead of feature lists.
Original ad angles to test without copying competitor assets.

best_practices: Use public, permitted data sources and keep notes on where each ad was found.
Compare several competitors to avoid overvaluing one brand strategy.
Translate patterns into original messages that match your brand and audience.
anti_patterns: Do not copy competitor ad copy, designs, or screenshots into your own campaign.
Do not treat ad frequency as proof of performance without supporting data.
Do not scrape private, restricted, or permission-protected advertising data.

faq.question: What ad sources can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It is written for public ad libraries such as Facebook Ad Library and LinkedIn ad research workflows.

faq.question: Does it automatically scrape websites?
faq.answer: The skill provides workflow guidance. Actual extraction depends on the tools, browser access, and permissions available to the user.

faq.question: Can it identify which ads perform best?
faq.answer: It can infer likely strengths from patterns and available signals, but it cannot prove performance without reliable platform data.

faq.question: Is it safe to use for competitor research?
faq.answer: Use it only with public sources and follow each platform terms, privacy rules, and intellectual property requirements.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompts support comparing several brands by message, format, audience, and positioning.

faq.question: What should users do with the insights?
faq.answer: Users should create original hypotheses, briefs, and test ideas instead of copying competitor campaigns.
